title: translation
content_html:
translation

The Moment without words is about trying to put feelings into language and reckoning with what changes along the way. The Library’s Image-Making as Translation extends that question to a photograph or painting. A phrase that passes between languages and a fleeting experience that becomes a picture both change in the passage. What survives, what is lost and what becomes possible because the medium has changed? without words · Image-Making as Translation

Reading note. Daoism. Chapter 26 of the Zhuangzi compares words with a device for catching fish. Once the fish is caught, the device can be set aside. In without words, the difficulty is getting a feeling into language at all. What might a reader or viewer take away from a phrase or picture once its particular wording or image recedes? Zhuangzi, 26, §13
